fullText:
DATA NETWORK EFFECTS ARE NOT REAL MOATS

I wrestled with data moats for 2 years before deciding this. 

(Note: Full episode on this, link below.)

My conclusions:

1. DATA NETWORK EFFECTS MOSTLY DO NOT EXIST.

The famous data flywheel is usually just ongoing customer improvement

which is a normal operating activity.

That’s great for performance. 

But it’s an operating flywheel, not a moat. 

And it’s usually a short term effect. 

2. MOST DATA SCALE IS AN EARLY STAGE EFFECT, NOT A PERMANENT ADVANTAGE.

Tesla drives better because it has more recorded miles

but I expect that edge to flatline as autonomous driving gets commoditized.

Such Scale advantages in data can give you an early advantage. 

But most non-proprietary is eventually replicated. 

3. WHAT MATTERS IS YOUR RATE OF LEARNING.

Data is just one input into how fast your business learns, adapts and builds in intelligence.

Superior Rate of learning and adaptation (based on data) is what gives you superior operating performance.

And maybe a moat. 

Outside of proprietary data, this could be a moat long term. 

***TAKEAWAYS FOR MANAGERS:

→ Audit your data this week and separate what is truly proprietary from what any rival could eventually have.

→ Pick one operation, such as customer service, and measure how quickly data improves it.

It is training its models on millions of digital objects in simulation.

A full embodied AI tech stack lets one multi purpose robot go into many settings.

Galbot is focused on Unstaffed retail cubes of 5-16 sqm

fullText:
Build your own harness, folks.

Reading papers like this makes me realize how underexplored harness engineering really is.

The authors find that on whole-repository migration, GPT-5.6 Sol goes from 6.5% to 31.0% when Codex is replaced with the HERMES harness, with the same model and effort setting.

The gain comes from the harness.

HERMES pairs each repository component with a resident LLM that knows its own code and dependencies. A dependency-aware step decides which components to activate, and a diagnosis step maps test failures back to the components that need changes.

Across four software engineering benchmarks, it beats matched baseline harnesses by 12.4 points on average.

With strong activation and diagnosis models, Qwen3-8B components come within 4.5 points of an all-GPT-5.6 Sol setup and cut Terminal-Bench 4.0 inference cost by 26.2%.

fullText:
Interesting paper from Sakana AI on memory for recurrent models.

Recurrent models are good at state tracking, but they usually keep everything in one hidden vector, so short-term computation and long-term storage compete for the same space.

The Continuous Memory Machine gives the model two memory matrices. One short-term memory tracks recent neuron activity, and the other long-term memory stores information for later steps. A Transformer reads and writes both at every step.

It builds on Sakana's Continuous Thought Machine and beats LSTM, DNC, RMC, and CTM baselines on copy, associative recall, sorting, few-shot regression, and maze solving. It also generalizes to longer inputs than earlier memory-augmented networks.

The attention maps show the model uses long-term memory for algorithmic and in-context tasks and skips it when the task does not need it.

Paper: https://t.co/89qZ1pbDTE
